Estimate total study cost

Source: R/estimate_cost.R
estimate_cost.Rd

Costs an MMS study from its design choices, as a variable cost plus a per-site cost:

  • Variable cost = total samples enrolled times the cost per sample (collection, laboratory testing, consumables, data management).

  • Site cost = the sum over sites of (fixed cost per site + transport cost per site). The fixed cost (training, equipment, administration) and the transport cost may each be given once for all sites or as one value per site.

Pairs with the design functions: take n and n_sites from a design function's result. To explore trade-offs, change n or n_sites and call it again. To cost several regions, call estimate_cost() once per region and add the totals. All monetary inputs and outputs are in one currency unit.

Usage

estimate_cost(
  n,
  cost_per_sample,
  n_sites = NULL,
  fixed_cost_per_site = 0,
  transport_cost_per_site = 0,
  budget = NULL
)

Arguments

n

Whole number. Total number of samples to be enrolled: $n from any design function (for design_difference(), the total across both groups).

cost_per_sample

Non-negative number. Variable cost per enrolled sample.

n_sites

Optional whole number. Total number of sites to cost: $n_sites from a design function (for design_difference(), sum(n_sites)). NULL (default) costs the samples only.

fixed_cost_per_site

Non-negative fixed cost per site: one number for every site, or one value per site (length n_sites). Default 0.

transport_cost_per_site

Non-negative transport cost per site: one number for every site, or one value per site. Default 0.

budget

Optional positive number. Total money available.

Value

A list with:

total_cost

variable_cost + site_cost.

variable_cost

n * cost_per_sample.

site_cost

Sum over sites of fixed plus transport cost; 0 when n_sites is NULL.

budget_remaining

budget - total_cost (negative if over budget), or NULL when no budget is given.

References

MMS-SD Study Design Workshop, budget-officer activity; Modules 2 and 7. https://mrc-ide.github.io/MMS-SD_workshop/

Examples

# Variable cost only
estimate_cost(n = 323, cost_per_sample = 50)
#> $total_cost
#> [1] 16150
#> 
#> $variable_cost
#> [1] 16150
#> 
#> $site_cost
#> [1] 0
#> 
#> $budget_remaining
#> NULL
#> 

# Same costs at every site (5,000 fixed + 1,000 transport per site)
estimate_cost(n = 600, cost_per_sample = 50, n_sites = 12,
              fixed_cost_per_site = 5000, transport_cost_per_site = 1000)
#> $total_cost
#> [1] 102000
#> 
#> $variable_cost
#> [1] 30000
#> 
#> $site_cost
#> [1] 72000
#> 
#> $budget_remaining
#> NULL
#> 

# A different fixed cost at each of 3 sites, checked against a budget
estimate_cost(n = 50, cost_per_sample = 10, n_sites = 3,
              fixed_cost_per_site = c(100, 200, 300), budget = 1500)
#> $total_cost
#> [1] 1100
#> 
#> $variable_cost
#> [1] 500
#> 
#> $site_cost
#> [1] 600
#> 
#> $budget_remaining
#> [1] 400
#> 

# Cost a design
des <- design_precision(prevalence = 0.15, moe = 0.05, n_per_site = 30, icc = 0.05)
estimate_cost(n = des$n, cost_per_sample = 50, n_sites = des$n_sites,
              fixed_cost_per_site = 5000, transport_cost_per_site = 1200)
#> $total_cost
#> [1] 123200
#> 
#> $variable_cost
#> [1] 24000
#> 
#> $site_cost
#> [1] 99200
#> 
#> $budget_remaining
#> NULL
#> 

# Cost a two-group design: design_difference() gives one n_sites per
# group, so add them up
des2 <- design_difference(0.10, 0.20, n_per_site = 30, icc = 0.05)
estimate_cost(n = des2$n, cost_per_sample = 50, n_sites = sum(des2$n_sites),
              fixed_cost_per_site = 5000)
#> $total_cost
#> [1] 221000
#> 
#> $variable_cost
#> [1] 51000
#> 
#> $site_cost
#> [1] 170000
#> 
#> $budget_remaining
#> NULL
#>
